title: Cluster Learning Dossier F02 Mechanical Maintenance: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.

bottom_line.text: No one owned the specification for the meter seal, so a locally bought O-ring with no specification or quality check became the regular part.
No procedure required a test to design pressure after the repair; the joint went back into service proved only at operating pressure.
The repair was planned and manned like routine work, with no independent check of the part, the method or the test.
Repeat seal failures on the same meter were fixed one at a time and never escalated for root cause.
The notification for the malfunction stayed open after the repair, so no close-out review looked at the part or the test.

items.decision: Give one function ownership of every pressure-part specification on the site and of approving any substitute.
options: Maintenance owns the specification and engineering approves substitutes
Engineering owns both, with maintenance and stores bound to its specification list
items.trade_offs: Ownership in maintenance sits close to the work; ownership in engineering keeps the design authority in one place. Either way the stores issue rule must follow it.

items.decision: Make a test to design pressure, or an engineered equivalent, a hold point before any pressure-boundary joint returns to service.
options: A written procedure with a hold point in the work order
The same, with the work-order system refusing release until a test result is entered
items.trade_offs: A system block is stronger than a procedure but needs the work-order system changed; both lengthen the return to service.

items.decision: Decide how a repeat failure of the same pressure item is escalated, and when an item is replaced rather than repaired again.
options: An automatic repeat-failure trigger in the maintenance system
A monthly repeat-failure review owned by a reliability role
items.trade_offs: A trigger catches every repeat but needs someone to own the analysis it opens; a review needs a role the site does not have today.

items.name: Pressure-boundary spares with a specification
items.measure: Share of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification and certificate on file.
items.deterioration: Any seal issued from stores without a specification reference.

items.name: Returns to service with a test record
items.measure: Share of pressure-boundary jobs returned to service with a recorded test result and witness signature.
items.deterioration: Any return to service on an operating-pressure check only.

items.name: Repeat failures reviewed
items.measure: Number of pressure items with a second corrective job within 12 months, and the share with a completed root-cause review.
items.deterioration: A third repair of the same item with no review.

sections.heading: S1 Profile
sections.intro: 194 findings name Mechanical Maintenance: 22 at L1, 36 at L2, 86 at L3 and 50 at L4. A finding can name roles at several tiers.

items.text: Every sub-division has a grounded learning except S13 Comparison, which is left out: no comparator report was supplied for this dossier. Findings where mechanical staff took part in the emergency response (the isolation decision and control-room competence) are covered in S6, because their learning belongs to other functions.

items.lesson: Fitting the locally bought O-ring had become the normal way to do the job, so it did not feel like a choice.
items.explanation: The substitute was used as a regular practice, with no specification or quality check to compare it against [FND-91B45FF9; FND-8C0BB623; EVD-8645]. It made sense at the time: the job had to be done, the original part could not be specified, and nothing in the system said stop.

items.lesson: With no written test, the crew used the check it had: pressurising to operating pressure.
items.explanation: After the gasket change on 18 September 2020 no hydro test was done; the system was pressurised to operating pressure and the meter went online the next day [FND-FD617187; FND-4944554C; EVD-2894; EVD-0185]. No procedure named a test pressure, so the quickest available check passed the joint.

items.lesson: Each seal failure was handled as a fresh repair.
items.explanation: The recurring failures were read as routine and repaired the same way, so the pattern started no review [FND-8DA35CA9; EVD-1494]. Nothing on the job record asked whether this was a repeat.

items.lesson: Notifications stayed open once the job was done.
items.explanation: Maintenance notifications were not closed after the work was completed [FND-56C66B96; FND-50775B5A; EVD-0591]. Closing them was not tied to returning the equipment, so leaving them open had no visible effect.

items.lesson: Painting was chosen for metal loss on a line with no corrosion allowance.
items.explanation: The July 2019 measurement found 1.03mm loss and heavy pitting, and painting was the corrective action [FND-5EC15274; EVD-2397]. The 2017 thickness findings had waited more than three years for a plan [FND-6D307E93; EVD-5527], so a painting job may have looked like progress.

items.lesson: The job was set up without the information it needed: no specification and no quality check for the part.
items.explanation: The original gasket specification was lost and no substitute specification or quality check existed, so the 18 September 2020 repair used a locally bought O-ring without engineering guidance [FND-82673283; FND-54180594; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: There was no procedure for taking a high-pressure meter back into service.
items.explanation: No SOP covered calibration and return to service of the high-pressure meters, and no hydrostatic test followed the gasket replacement [FND-9174A5B0; FND-FDFA6FF5; EVD-2894].

items.lesson: The repair was planned and manned like routine work.
items.explanation: The job was planned without the specification, part quality control, hydrostatic test or notification closure, and no material or quality verification roles were assigned [FND-2FAB8D51; FND-28F8790B; EVD-8645; EVD-2894].

items.lesson: A meter that kept failing stayed in service.
items.explanation: The meter was kept in service across three gasket replacements in 22 months [FND-69067A1C; EVD-1494; EVD-0591].

items.lesson: A damaged flame-proof lamp stayed in service in the hazardous area.
items.explanation: The lamp had three bolts missing and its glass case open, and was not repaired before ignition [FND-784A23E4; EVD-6916].

items.lesson: The metering drawing did not match the field.
items.explanation: The original drawing was lost, the vendor replacement was not checked or approved, and the valve and meter configuration did not match [FND-72DCEE68; FND-733F5A1A; EVD-0933].

items.lesson: Supervisors had no rule to enforce on the seal, and the substitution became the modelled norm.
items.explanation: Supervision tolerated and modelled the O-ring substitution, and authorised it as a regular practice, without any specification or quality control to hold it to [FND-A443D288; FND-42BEF461; FND-852B7EC7; EVD-8645]. What a supervisor should refuse: a pressure part with no specification behind it.

items.lesson: Return to service was authorised without the test, and the omission was not caught.
items.explanation: The meter was released without a hydrostatic test, and no one identified or corrected the omission before it went back online [FND-5919B328; FND-8ACDE078; EVD-2894; EVD-0185]. What a supervisor should see before signing: the test result and who witnessed it.

items.lesson: Pressure-boundary work was ordered without an independent check or a job safety analysis.
items.explanation: The job was authorised with no independent quality control, inspection or permit verification, and no formal risk assessment [FND-F8C125D5; FND-63B6D260; EVD-5105].

items.lesson: Repeat failures did not reach a supervisor as a pattern.
items.explanation: The recurring seal failures were not escalated into a root-cause investigation or a corrective engineering change [FND-110F964C; FND-D14B8424; FND-FEC84761; EVD-1494].

items.lesson: The notification for the repair was never closed or reviewed by supervision.
items.explanation: The notification raised on 17 September 2020 was left open with no supervisory closure review [FND-FA807C69; FND-AE60859C; EVD-0591].

items.lesson: Integrity findings were accepted without a corrective plan.
items.explanation: Supervision accepted painting for the July 2019 pitting and left the 2017 thickness findings without a corrective plan [FND-ABDADA0C; FND-C6992EAF; EVD-2397; EVD-5527].

items.lesson: Calibration work had no checklist, and the signed record did not show a setting change.
items.explanation: No checklist was provided for high-pressure calibration jobs, and the December 2019 setting change was not in the signed documents [FND-D58142C9; FND-E94D563C; EVD-2506].

items.lesson: Permit and job safety plan gaps were left uncorrected.
items.explanation: Missing permits were not tracked and job safety plans were not attached, and supervision did not correct either [FND-A3D2773A; FND-EFC192D7; EVD-5105].

items.lesson: No one owned pressure-part specifications or the approval of substitutes.
items.explanation: No role owned the gasket specification, the quality control of its purchase or the authority to approve a substitute, and the organisation came to trust the locally bought O-ring as a valid seal [FND-23139BF9; FND-B56701CA; FND-D40839C1; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: The organisation trusted operating pressure to prove a repaired joint.
items.explanation: There was no return-to-service SOP for high-pressure meter work, and operating-pressure pressurisation was taken as enough [FND-50C7319E; FND-86CB3683; EVD-2894].

items.lesson: Safety-critical maintenance was resourced like routine work.
items.explanation: The job was manned with no independent quality-control role, test witness or closing supervisor [FND-615DB819; EVD-2894; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: There was no reliability programme for ageing pressure equipment.
items.explanation: The meter was left to routine resealing, with no manufacturer spares, root-cause work or replacement programme, and kept in service with a 1986 pressure boundary [FND-1A251687; FND-55F68376; EVD-1494; EVD-0064].

items.lesson: The change procedure existed but was not used.
items.explanation: The MOC policy was not implemented after 2018, which allowed an unapproved material substitution [FND-F7FE8463; EVD-2986].

items.lesson: Electrical equipment in hazardous areas was maintained on breakdown.
items.explanation: A breakdown-maintenance philosophy for flame-proof equipment in Zone 1 left a damaged fitting in service [FND-1280E788; EVD-9999; EVD-6916].

items.lesson: The inspection programme ran off its schedule with no escalation.
items.explanation: The four-year thickness cycle was not kept, and the 2017 findings stayed unplanned [FND-A3DCEBD8; FND-C4842890; EVD-8307].

items.lesson: Backup fire-water pumps were left degraded.
items.explanation: Two diesel fire-water pumps were under maintenance and one had an undiagnosed tripping fault [FND-B955FBD6; FND-DF7337F2; EVD-2432].

items.text: Mechanical Maintenance shares findings with almost every function. The largest seams are with Operations & Control Room (71 shared findings), Asset Integrity, Corrosion & Inspection (40), Engineering, Design, Documents & MOC (34), Work Management & Planning (27) and Materials Management (27) [FND-4944554C; FND-69067A1C; FND-137BC719; FND-1662466D; FND-2CEE8915].

items.lesson: The seal fell between maintenance and stores: each could take the part as settled by the other.
items.explanation: Stores bought locally available O-rings and maintenance fitted them, with no specification or approval on either side [FND-23139BF9; FND-6B3A6492; EVD-8645].

items.lesson: Operations accepted the meter back with no test record to look at.
items.explanation: Return to service after the gasket change went ahead without design-pressure validation, and operations took the meter online the next day [FND-491EDE74; FND-3AB996FC; EVD-0185].
items.owner: Mechanical Maintenance (F02) with Operations & Control Room (F01)

items.lesson: The closure of the job sat with no one between maintenance and work management.
items.explanation: The notification close-out had no assigned review owner and was left open after the repair [FND-646BAC1F; FND-678E51A3; EVD-0591].
items.owner: Mechanical Maintenance (F02) with Work Management & Planning (F08)

items.lesson: Repeat failures and wall-loss findings sat between maintenance and integrity, with no reliability owner.
items.explanation: Reliability planning across the seal-replacement history was missing, and the 2017 thickness findings had no corrective plan [FND-AC8FBB26; FND-1F685360; EVD-1494; EVD-5527].

items.lesson: A change made through a work order never reached engineering.
items.explanation: The decision to use locally bought O-rings was never recorded or communicated under MOC [FND-5A5F6AB3; FND-CAF9833D; EVD-2986].

items.lesson: Mechanical staff on the night shift were part of an isolation response that had no criteria.
items.explanation: The plan gave the control room no isolation decision criteria, and the night-shift crew included mechanical staff with general training only [FND-314D34C5; FND-2AA87E93; EVD-4052; EVD-5634].
items.owner: Emergency Planning & Command (F09b) with Mechanical Maintenance (F02)

items.failure_mode: No specification for the seal and no owner to re-establish it.
items.fix: Re-establish the seal design and stock only certified parts against it.

items.failure_mode: No procedure required a test to design pressure; operating pressure only.
items.fix: Block release of pressure-boundary jobs in the work-order system until a test result is entered.

items.failure_mode: No independent check of part, method or test was manned.
items.fix: A safety-critical work category that adds inspection, witness and close-out steps.

items.barrier: inspection and integrity (repeat failures on ageing equipment)
items.failure_mode: No reliability review of repeat failures; the same repair each time.
items.fix: An automatic repeat-failure trigger and a repair-or-replace decision per item.

items.failure_mode: Thickness surveys ran six years apart against a four-year schedule, without baseline data.
items.fix: Schedule inspections in the maintenance system with automatic escalation when overdue.

lint_ok.reason: the scheduling and escalation change is the system fix for the inspection programme; the engineering fix for the wall loss itself is in the barrier-learnings pack

sections.heading: S8 Precursors
sections.intro: The dated signals that reached Mechanical Maintenance. A year-only date means the source gives only the year.

events.text: Pipe-wall thickness measured in 2011, then not again until 2017, against a four-year schedule.
events.response: None recorded: the schedule slipped with no escalation.
events.knowable_then: The schedule and the dates of the last measurements were in the inspection records.

events.text: The two condensate meters are cleaned, serviced and calibrated: the first entry in the seal-repair history of the meter that later failed.
events.response: Routine service; no review of the seal design recorded.
events.knowable_then: The service record was in the maintenance history.

events.text: The same meter is cleaned and its gasket changed, with a locally bought O-ring as the usual substitute.
events.response: Repaired like for like; no root-cause review or escalation recorded.
events.knowable_then: A repeat job on the same meter was in the maintenance history, and the substitute O-ring practice was known to the crew and its supervisors.

events.text: A spot ultrasonic measurement finds 1.03mm wall loss with heavy pitting on a segment of the 36-inch pipeline at the gas terminal.
events.knowable_then: The measurement and the line's design thickness were on record when the painting-only repair was chosen.

events.text: During calibration a setting on the meter is changed and later changed back, with no mention in the signed calibration documents.
events.response: None recorded: no checklist was used for the job.
events.knowable_then: Only the calibration team knew of the change; the signed record did not show it.

sections.heading: S9 Tier messages
sections.intro: From the register's tier messages for the seal (LR-01) and the return-to-service test (LR-02).

items.text: If you cannot confirm a seal or gasket matches the specification for a pressure part, stop and ask for the spec. Do not fit 'what we normally use'. After any work that opens a pressure boundary, ask: what test proves this joint, and who witnessed it? Write the answer on the job record.

Before signing off pressure-boundary work, check the part against a written specification. No spec means no sign-off. Do not accept equipment back from maintenance without a recorded leak/pressure test to the written test pressure.

Find every pressure-boundary item with no specification on file and re-establish it (OEM, reverse engineering or an engineered substitute). Write and issue a return-to-service procedure for high-pressure equipment that sets test type, test pressure and witness.

Give one named function ownership of pressure-part specifications and of approving any substitute. Treat return to service after pressure-boundary work as a hold point that operations must accept in writing.
Ask for assurance that legacy (pre-2000) pressure equipment has current part specifications and controlled spares.

items.change: Re-establish the seal design for the meter flange (OEM data or engineered equivalent) and stock only certified parts against that specification; quarantine non-conforming seals.
items.indicator: Share of critical pressure-boundary spares with a specification and certificate on file (target 100%).

items.change: Make the stores system refuse to issue a pressure-boundary seal without a specification reference and an approved-substitute record.
items.indicator: Number of pressure-part issues blocked or referred for engineering approval per quarter, and their closure time.

items.change: Survey legacy equipment for lost specifications and plan replacement of meters that can no longer be maintained to specification.
items.indicator: Percentage of legacy items surveyed; number with a replacement or re-specification decision recorded.

items.change: Issue a return-to-service procedure for pressure-boundary work stating test medium, test pressure (design-based), hold time and independent witness, with a hold point in the work order.
items.indicator: Share of pressure-boundary work orders closed with a recorded test result and witness signature (audited sample).
items.why_not_stronger: Paired with the engineering block in the work-order system below; the procedure sets the test the block enforces.

lint_ok.reason: Paired with the engineering block in the work-order system below; the procedure sets the test the block enforces.

items.change: Configure the work-order system so a pressure-boundary job cannot be closed or the equipment released to operations until a test result is entered.
items.indicator: Number of attempted closures blocked for missing test data; trend to zero over two quarters.

items.change: Introduce a safety-critical maintenance category in work planning that automatically adds inspection, test-witness and close-out review steps.
items.indicator: Share of safety-critical jobs with all verification steps signed by someone other than the performer.

items.change: Require a job safety analysis and permit review for any work opening a hydrocarbon pressure boundary, separate from the maintenance notification.
items.indicator: Audited share of pressure-boundary jobs with a completed JSA attached in the work system.
items.why_not_stronger: A job safety analysis is a planning control; the engineering part of this learning is the safety-critical work category above.

lint_ok.reason: A job safety analysis is a planning control; the engineering part of this learning is the safety-critical work category above.

items.change: Set an automatic repeat-failure trigger in the CMMS (e.g. two corrective jobs on one tag in 12 months) that opens a root-cause investigation task.
items.indicator: Number of bad actors flagged per quarter and share with a completed root-cause analysis within 60 days.

rows: Recognise a pressure-boundary part with no specification on file and stop the job until one is provided; record the test that proves the joint and who witnessed it.
Check the part against a written specification and the test record before signing off pressure-boundary work; raise a root-cause request when the same item fails twice.
Plan pressure-boundary work as safety-critical, with inspection and witness points; run the repeat-failure report.
Hold ownership of pressure-part specifications in one function, and treat return to service as a hold point.
Any site with legacy pressure equipment whose original part data is lost
Any pressure-boundary work returned to service
Any high-consequence job resourced as routine work
Any maintenance system that does not count repeats
Sites using the same work-management system and closure practice

limits: Written from the labels and short texts of all 194 F02 findings and the full text of the highest-rated; the register's grouping of findings into learnings was reused.
No comparator report was supplied, so S13 is left out.
Owners and dates for the decisions and recommendations are for the organisation to set.
